svg.aria-label: How to write さようなら: 5 letters, さ, よ, う, な, ら, one after another
svg.title: Writing さようなら
svg.desc: 5 letters written one after another: さ, よ, う, な, ら (japanese). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: さ: KanjiVG, kanji/03055.svg, hiragana さ (U+3055 HIRAGANA LETTER SA), three stroke paths kvg:03055-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03055.svg>; よ: Sirgazil, Hiragana よ stroke order animation.gif, hiragana よ, 26 frames, 2.6 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009; corrected first-stroke direction 4 January 2012) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hiragana_%E3%82%88_stroke_order_animation.gif>; う: KanjiVG, kanji/03046.svg, hiragana う (U+3046 HIRAGANA LETTER U), two stroke paths kvg:03046-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03046.svg>; な: Sirgazil, Hiragana な stroke order animation.gif, hiragana な, 32 frames, 3.2 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hiragana_%E3%81%AA_stroke_order_animation.gif>; ら: KanjiVG, kanji/03089.svg, hiragana ら (U+3089 HIRAGANA LETTER RA), two stroke paths kvg:03089-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03089.svg>. Source notes on variation: さ: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the bar drawn left to right, rising slightly; s2 starts above the bar, slants down to the right through it and hooks back to the left at its foot without lifting; s3 starts at the left, curves down and runs out to the right along the base. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. よ: The CC0 animation draws よ in two pen-down runs with one lift. Its corrected first stroke moves left to right; the second descends through that bar, turns left, and continues clockwise around the broad lower loop to the rightward finish. The learner path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans JP subset; handwritten loop width varies, but the two-run order remains the same. う: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the short top stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down that the print glyph does not show; s2 starts at the left, rises to the right along the top, rounds the right side and sweeps away to the lower left. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. な: The CC0 animation draws な in four pen-down runs with three lifts: the upper-left horizontal, crossing left-falling stem, short upper-right diagonal, then the lower-right stem continuing around the loop and out to the right. The learner path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans JP subset; handwritten diagonal angle and loop size vary, but the four-run order remains the same. ら: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the short top stroke drawn from left to right, ending in a small turn down that the print glyph does not show; s2 starts on the left below it, runs down, turns at its foot without lifting, rises to the right over the top of the bowl, rounds its right side and finishes at the lower left. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 5 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 4 movements
Letter 2 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 3 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 4 of 5 — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 5 movements
Letter 5 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03055.svg, hiragana さ (U+3055 HIRAGANA LETTER SA), three stroke paths kvg:03055-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 2: stroke order after Sirgazil, Hiragana よ stroke order animation.gif, hiragana よ, 26 frames, 2.6 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009; corrected first-stroke direction 4
Letter 3: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03046.svg, hiragana う (U+3046 HIRAGANA LETTER U), two stroke paths kvg:03046-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 4: stroke order after Sirgazil, Hiragana な stroke order animation.gif, hiragana な, 32 frames, 3.2 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009)
Letter 5: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03089.svg, hiragana ら (U+3089 HIRAGANA LETTER RA), two stroke paths kvg:03089-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
